title: Calixtus: those who do this receive greater aids
source_text: VIII. Hoc autem qui faciunt, eos Deus, secundum hujus Doctoris mentem, majoribus auxiliis dignatur, ut intelligant verbum, ex eo peccata sua agnoscant, & promissionibus Evangelicis fidem habeant: non quidem quod ista qualiscunque opera tantae sit dignitatis aut meriti, sed quod suo verbo Deus eum velit honorem haberi, hunc ordinem servari, & hoc ab homine praestari, priusquam ipse majora & specialiora, & suo genere supernaturalia suppeditet auxilia.
pass_a_gloss: VIII. But those who do this, God, according to this Doctor's mind, deems worthy of greater aids, that they may understand the word, from it acknowledge their sins, & have faith in the Gospel promises: not indeed that this work of whatever kind is of so great dignity or merit, but because God wills that this honour be had to his word, this order be kept, & this be performed by man, before he himself supplies greater & more special, & in their kind supernatural aids.
pass_b_english: Thesis VIII. In this doctor's view, God judges those who do this worthy of greater aids, so that they understand the word, recognize their sins from it, and put faith in the promises of the Gospel.

This is not because such effort, whatever its worth, has any great dignity or merit. It is because God wants his word honoured in this way, wants this order kept, and wants the person to do this much before God himself provides greater and more particular aids, supernatural in kind.

lemmas.gloss: not indeed that this work of whatever kind is of so great dignity or merit
supplies aids supernatural in their kind

choices.why: The Roman school's division of grace, kept in its technical terms throughout the locus.
